Subject: Capacity readiness checklist & agreed next steps

Hi Priya / Liam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the performance / SLO items we discussed and the actions we agreed to take. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level SLOs you called out:
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms for median response lengths (~256 tokens); p99 target <= 450 ms for same profile.
- Concurrency: baseline 120 concurrent sessions with sustained bursts up to ~600 concurrent requests for 5–10 minute windows.
- Throughput: steady-state token throughput ~1.2M tokens/hour during business hours; bursts up to ~4M tokens/hour.
- Streaming: required for the client UX (partial token streaming to browser); first-byte streaming latency target p50 < 60 ms.
- Availability during release windows is critical (you mentioned 99.9% uptime objective during peak hours).

Autoscale / warm pool constraints we noted:
- Cold start: acceptable scale-up from zero to supporting 50 concurrent sessions in < 30s.
- Warm pool: you prefer a small pre-warmed pool for fast bursts — suggested starting point 10% of baseline instances (we'll bench this).
- Queueing: short transient queueing acceptable (<2s) but request rejects need to be extremely rare; prefer graceful degradation with fallbacks.

Immediate next steps (owner in parens):
1) Redwood will run a custom benchmark with your (sample) load profile — propose Wed 2 Dec or Thu 3 Dec (Rishi). Attachment: redwood_capacity_template.xlsx (we'll use this for the traffic shape).
2) Rishi to propose warm-pool sizing and autoscale policy tuned to your diurnal pattern (Rishi).
3) Redwood to provide a short runbook for streaming integration and client-side reconnect behavior (Monica).
4) Priya to confirm the traffic sample, SOC2 / VPC requirements, and available windows for benchmark (Priya).

Attachments: redwood_capacity_template.xlsx (traffic shapes), suggested template for benchmark job.

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm the benchmark slot.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — clear recap and appreciated. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed SLOs: p95 <= 200 ms for short-form outputs (<=256 tokens). For longer completions (~1k tokens) we accept higher p95 but want consistent streaming behavior.
- Bursts: typical release spikes historically last 3–8 minutes; peak concurrency has reached ~720 for short windows during releases (we flagged 600 earlier as our safe starting point).
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed VPC required for production; we have an internal SCC who will send the questionnaire next week.
- Benchmark windows: prefer Thu 3 Dec 09:00–11:00 PST or Fri 4 Dec 13:00–15:00 PST. Please advise which works.

One question: for streaming, do you support sending partial tokens over websockets and measuring first-byte latencies separately from end-to-end response latencies? We'll need metrics that map to our frontend timing.

I'll also attach a small traffic sample and some historic histograms once my infra team is back online (should be by EOD today).

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics

Priya / team — quick tech notes ahead of the benchmark so expectations are aligned.

1) Warm-pool strategy: based on the numbers you gave, our recommendation for the benchmark is:
   - Reserved baseline capacity: 8 gpus (Nvidia A100 equivalent) to cover the 120 baseline concurrency for the model family you described.
   - Warm pool: start at 10% of baseline instances (we'll pre-warm ~1 instance group that can add capacity in < 10s per instance) and iterate.

2) Scale-up times / cold-start: scale-up to 50 concurrent sessions from zero will depend heavily on model size and container init times; in our internal tests with quantized variants we can hit ~25–35s. We'll capture the cold-start distribution during the run.

3) Queueing & smoothing: to avoid rejects we suggest allowing a short transient queue (configurable, default 2s) and enabling short-lived token-level batching so streaming first bytes are not delayed significantly. If your UI tolerates 1–2s initial queueing we can reduce overall rejects during sharp spikes.

4) Streaming: Redwood supports websocket streaming for partial tokens. We'll measure both first-byte (first-stream) and full-response p50/p95/p99. For frontend mapping we'll provide a separate telemetry stream that emits first-byte timestamps so you can instrument your UX metrics directly.

5) Success criteria for benchmark:
   - p95 full-response <= 200 ms for 256-token profile under baseline load
   - first-byte p50 < 60 ms for streaming path
   - <0.5% request rejects during a 10-minute synthetic spike to 3x baseline concurrency

Attaching a quick latency histogram from a recent test to set expectations. We'll run the benchmark using Stephanie's spreadsheet and share raw logs + perf dashboard.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
